svg.title: A name is a sticky note. Assignment moves the note.
svg.desc: Two sticky notes labelled a and b both point at one list object with refcount 2 and cells 1, 2, 3 and a dashed 4 appended through a. Beside it, the picture most people hold — two separate list objects — is crossed out in red, and the contrasting case a = a + [4] is drawn as a genuinely new object. Below, the CPython object header is drawn field by field with measured sizes, and six bars compare per-record memory for a million records from 268 bytes in a dict down to 28 bytes columnar.
svg.text: A name is a sticky note. Assignment moves the note.
one object, seen through two names
two objects. There is only one.
but a = a + [4] really does build a new one:
the note was peeled off and re-stuck. b never moved.
every object carries this header first
int 28 B · float 24 B · empty list 56 B · empty dict 64 B
b never appeared in that append line. One
object, two notes. Assignment moves a note - it
...and if two objects point at each other?
same data. The container is the cost.
